title: Data Analyst – Dashboard & Insights
description: About CSRBOX CSRBOX is India’s leading CSR knowledge and impact intelligence-driven media cum social impact advisory platform. It works as an enabler to create corporate-non-profit, corporate-corporate, and corporate-government collaborations. Our biggest strength is our research and consulting team which maps over 4000 CSR projects and 1500 companies' CSR portfolios every year. We have a strong CSR Implementation Vertical with the name BharatCares, which works with companies and CSR foundations for their CSR projects for underprivileged communities across livelihoods, skill development, education, health, and environment thematic. A few of our corporate clients are ICICI Bank, SKF Ltd., Bosch India, IBM India, Diageo, DP World, Future Generali, Airbus, Arvind, LG Electronics, Hero MotoCorp, Sandvik, Vastu Housing Finance, DCM Shriram, L&T, etc. For more information, visit: www.csrbox.org Curious about what Life @ CSRBOX looks like? Explore: https://csrbox.org/Life-at-CSRBOX/ Job Position Data Analyst – Dashboard & Insights Location: Ahmedabad Salary: INR 5.50 LPA to 7.20 LPA (Depending on Experience) Position Overview We are looking for a Data Analyst – Dashboard & Insights who will be responsible for transforming program, CSR, project, and organizational data into interactive dashboards, visual reports, and actionable insights. The role will work closely with internal teams such as CSR Programs, Consulting, Knowledge Management, Finance, HR, and Leadership to understand reporting requirements, organize data, develop dashboards, and ensure that decision-makers have access to accurate and meaningful information. The ideal candidate should have strong hands-on experience in Power BI/Tableau, SQL, Excel, data visualization, data cleaning, and dashboard development, along with the ability to understand business and social-impact datasets. Key Responsibilities Dashboard Development & Data Visualization Design, develop, and maintain interactive dashboards for CSRBOX's internal and external reporting requirements. Build dashboards covering areas such as CSR projects, beneficiaries, program performance, geography, budgets, outcomes, impact indicators, and organizational KPIs. Develop dashboards using Power BI, Tableau, Looker Studio, or similar BI tools. Create intuitive visualizations, charts, maps, KPIs, scorecards, and drill-down reports. Ensure dashboards are user-friendly, responsive, and suitable for both management and operational teams. Data Management & Analysis Collect, clean, validate, transform, and structure data from multiple sources. Work with large datasets from Excel, Google Sheets, databases, APIs, CRM/HRIS systems, and program management platforms. Identify data inconsistencies, missing values, duplicates, and quality issues and coordinate with relevant teams for resolution. Perform descriptive and diagnostic analysis to identify trends, patterns, gaps, and opportunities. Develop automated data pipelines and refresh mechanisms wherever feasible. SQL & Database Management Write SQL queries to extract, join, filter, aggregate, and analyze data. Work with relational databases and maintain structured datasets required for reporting. Support the creation and optimization of data models for dashboarding. Ensure appropriate data definitions and consistency across different reports and dashboards. Business & Program Insights Translate business and program requirements into meaningful data solutions. Work with program teams to identify relevant KPIs and impact indicators. Generate insights from CSR and social-impact data to support strategic decision-making. Identify trends in project performance, beneficiary reach, fund utilization, geographic coverage, and other relevant indicators. Present analytical findings in a simple and actionable manner to non-technical stakeholders. Reporting & MIS Develop recurring MIS reports and management dashboards. Automate repetitive reporting processes to reduce manual effort. Establish standardized reporting formats and data definitions. Maintain documentation for dashboards, KPIs, data sources, and calculation methodologies. Ensure timely delivery of periodic reports to internal stakeholders. Stakeholder Collaboration Work closely with business, program, consulting, finance, HR, and leadership teams to understand their data requirements. Conduct requirement-gathering discussions and convert requirements into dashboard specifications. Train relevant team members on dashboard usage and interpretation. Provide ongoing support and improvements based on user feedback. Required Skills Strong hands-on experience with Power BI or Tableau. Strong knowledge of SQL. Advanced proficiency in MS Excel / Google Sheets, including Pivot Tables, lookup functions, Power Query, and data analysis. Understanding of data modelling, ETL processes, and dashboard architecture. Strong knowledge of data visualization and dashboard design principles. Ability to work with large and complex datasets. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills. Ability to translate business requirements into data-driven solutions. Good understanding of data quality and validation processes. Strong communication and stakeholder management skills. Good to Have Experience with Python for data analysis and automation. Experience with Google BigQuery, PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, or similar databases. Experience working with APIs and automated data integrations. Familiarity with GIS/geospatial visualization and map-based dashboards. Experience working with CSR, ESG, sustainability, NGO, development-sector, or social-impact datasets. Understanding of CSR reporting, SDGs, impact measurement, or program monitoring and evaluation. Experience with cloud-based data platforms and data warehouses. Education Bachelor's degree in Data Analytics, Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, Information Technology, Economics, Engineering, or a related discipline. Candidates with a postgraduate qualification in Data Analytics, Business Analytics, Statistics, or a related field will be preferred. Experience 2–5 years of relevant experience in data analytics, business intelligence, MIS, dashboard development, or data visualization. Candidates with demonstrated experience in independently developing and managing Power BI/Tableau dashboards from raw data to final insights will be preferred. Why Join CSRBOX? Work at the intersection of data, CSR, sustainability, and social impact. Build data products that support large-scale social-impact programs. Work with diverse datasets across sectors and geographies. Collaborate with corporates, NGOs, government stakeholders, and development partners. Opportunity to build and scale CSR and impact analytics capabilities within a growing organization. How to apply Please fill out the Google Form: https://forms.gle/QxBm8hPr8YMqM7D9A Note: Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

title: Manager - Learning Strategy and Projects

Strategic thinker finds connections to bigger picture and drives valuable experiences and conversations with members. Knowledge of and experience in delivering edtech powered learning projects Comfortable speaking in front of small and large groups. A sense-maker: able to perceive emerging industry trends and translate them into content and/or learning experiences. Proven experience as an adaptive and collaborative member, willing to take on new projects and support initiatives that build an enterprise. Strong networking and interpersonal skills. Openness to new ideas; a creative and innovative mind energetically searching for new solutions. Inquisitive, flexible with entrepreneurial spirit and the ability to thrive in a fast-paced environment. A passion for learning and continuous improvement. title: Assistant General Manager

Conceptualize and effect partnerships with relevant government, UN, private sector and NGO and other relevant stakeholders. title: Project Lead - Early Childhood Education
description: About Central Square Foundation Central Square Foundation is a non-profit organisation working with the vision of ensuring quality school education for all children in India. Since 2012, we have been partnering with the government and ecosystem stakeholders to improve the learning outcomes of children, especially from low-income communities. We are driven by our mission to enable the school education system to adopt solutions that are scalable, sustainable and effective, so that all children get equal access to opportunities needed for their better future. About the position Early Childhood Education (ECE) refers to the pre-primary years, between the ages of 3 and 6, before a child enters Grade 1. Research across economics, neuroscience and education has shown that 90% of brain development happens before the age of 5, and that the quality of these years shapes a child’s schooling, health and income for life. The National Education Policy 2020 calls for three years of pre-primary education for every child. CSF partners with state governments and academic bodies to support the institutionalisation of developmentally appropriate pre-primary education within government school systems through curriculum, teacher preparation, classroom resources and implementation support. Key Responsibilities: Build playbooks and provide implementation support: Consolidate programme design, classroom practice and field learning into playbooks and resource packages a state can adopt. Test and refine these with state teams and government counterparts, and support states with the operationalisation of pre-primary classes at scale. Nurture ecosystem partnerships: Build relationships with non-profits, funders and multilateral organisations in early childhood education, and turn shared interests into joint work on standards and teacher preparation. Engage on policy: Draft briefs and notes that help central and state policymakers plan and fund the early years within national programmes such as NIPUN Bharat, and represent CSF in sector forums. Drive the evidence agenda: Identify gaps in current literature and practice, frame the questions worth answering, and work with CSF's research team on pilots and studies to address them. Support fundraising: Write proposals and support funder conversations for the ECE workstream. Lead delivery and people: Set the roadmap, review structures and project management processes for central ECE workstreams. Guide project managers, consultants and vendors and develop them through direct feedback. Required Qualifications, Skills, and Abilities Experience Across Multiple Kinds of Work: 7 - 9 years in education, development, public policy or consulting, including close work with government systems and some exposure to ECE programmes. A Master's in Education, Public Policy, Social Sciences or Management preferred. Working Effectively Within Government Systems: Direct experience with senior officials and department leadership, including a practical grasp of how decisions are made, and what it takes to move them. Comparable experience with partner organisations, funders and multilateral agencies. Synthesis and Communication: The ability to synthesize evidence, field observations, and practitioner input into policy briefs and white papers. Fluency in English and Hindi: Both spoken and written, at a standard that supports drafting for a ministry and contextualizing for a state workshop. Ownership from Strategy to Delivery: A record of running several workstreams at once without loss of quality, and of guiding junior colleagues and consultants to high-quality work. A Hands-On Temperament: Suited to a small team with evolving priorities and frequent travel to field locations, and comfortable operating without a settled plan. title: Senior Program Manager – Creches
description: About Organization: Ekjut is a non-profit voluntary organization of India. It’s partnering communities are the indigenous people, people living in the underserved districts and the urban deprived communities. Ekjut works on the theme of Survive, Thrive and Transform. For more details about the organisation, please visit the website http://www.ekjutindia.org/. About the Project: The Rural Creche Initiative project in Ekjut supports creches or day care centers in rural areas of Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh and Odisha. These creches or day care centers open 6 days a week for children in the 6–36 months age group where they stay for 7-8 hours a day. In the creche, children get 1 cooked meal and 2 cooked snacks with 1boiled egg daily, age-appropriate early childhood development activities, they are in a safe secured and hygienic environment managed by 2 trained creche workers from the same village. Currently, Ekjut manages more than 300 creches under this initiative in the 3 states. Vacancy details Senior Program Manager – Creches Base Location: Gumla District of Jharkhand Area of Work: Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh and Odisha Reports to: Team Lead Supports and Supervises: Program Manager, Training Coordinator, Cluster Coordinators, Capacity Building Officers, Safety & Security Officer Purpose of the Role/Why this job role: The Senior Program Manager will provide strategic and managerial leadership to ensure the smooth functioning of the crèche initiative for children aged 6 months to 3 years. This role will focus on supportive supervision, assure program quality, timely documentation and reporting, seamless supply chain management, identify the gaps for capacity building, provide critical inputs and take initiative for continuous improvement of the initiative. Key Responsibilities: Provide overall leadership, coordination, support and guidance to all creche-related staff and functions across all the states that Ekjut manages creches under this initiative. Ensure smooth operations across all crèches with a focus on quality child care, safety, and early childhood development outcomes and reporting of the same. Strengthen systems for supervision, quality standards, and handholding support to teams engaged in the initiative. Strengthen data collection, monitoring system, and use evidence for decision-making and continuous program improvement. Facilitate cross-learning, knowledge sharing, and capacity building of team members. Provide critical inputs in programme designing bringing innovation, and ensuring smooth and consistent flow of supplies. Build and maintain effective partnerships with local communities, donor representatives, and other stakeholders. Review programme progress regularly and ensure timely reporting to senior management and donors. Identify gaps, risks, challenges through regular field visit and observations and support the team in problem-solving and course correction as required to meet program objectives. Ensure child safety, protection, and compliance standards across all crèches and the teams. Overseeing, managing and implementing rural crèche policies and procedures. Qualifications & Experience: Postgraduate in Social Work, Rural Management, Child Development, Public Health, Management or related field. Minimum 8-12 years of relevant experience in program management, preferably in child development, health, nutrition or community-based initiatives. Strong leadership, people management, and supportive supervision skills. Experience in large-scale field operations or multi-site program management. Experience in capacity building of FLF. Demonstrated ability to engage with tribal communities and work in rural/remote areas. Excellent communication, coordination, and problem-solving skills. Skill in nurturing collaboration with multiple stakeholders (community leaders, local govt, donors. Competencies: Strategic thinking with operational efficiency. Team building and mentorship. Commitment to child rights, safety, and holistic development. Flexibility, patience, and ability to navigate complex situations. Willing to travel extensively. This work involves field travel of 2-3 weeks per month. Remuneration: CTC 10-12 Lakhs per annum (CTC includes EPF, Gratuity, Taxes) Note: Applicants especially women and those from marginalized communities are encouraged to apply. Ability to link with the community and community-based organizations. Applications are received on rolling basis until fulfilled. Call or WhatsApp from Applicant will not be entertained. Only shortlisted applicants will receive a response from Ekjut HR (Human Resources) or authorized officer How to apply Interested candidates can submit their Updated CV, mentioning the position in email subject she/he is applying for the position in the subject line on email: ekjuthr@gmail.com till 07 th September 2026 .

title: Research Specialist - Action Research
description: About International Water Management Institute The International Water Management Institute (IWMI) is an international, research-for-development organization that works with governments, civil society and the private sector to solve water problems in developing countries and scale up solutions. Through partnership, IWMI combines research on the sustainable use of water and land resources, knowledge services and products with capacity strengthening, dialogue and policy analysis to support implementation of water management solutions for agriculture, ecosystems, climate change and inclusive economic growth. Headquartered in Colombo, Sri Lanka, IWMI is a CGIAR Research Centre with offices in 15 countries and a global network of scientists operating in more than 55 countries. DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES: Main Purpose of Job: Plan, design, oversee, and monitor research activities, including developing field action sites, protocols, data collection, analysis, and interpretation, based on a defined research plan to achieve project objectives and development outcomes. Gather and synthesize information and literature to design studies, experiments, surveys, related to action research ensuring alignment with the research outline provided. Design and implement monitoring system to assess the performance and impacts of agrivoltaics and action research projects. Provide support in vocational training activities (e.g., crafts, basic production tasks, life skills, pre‑vocational tasks), under the guidance of the vocational trainer/special educator. Help CWSN with personal care and self‑help needs where required (mobility, toileting, dressing, eating/drinking) in a dignified and respectful manner, following safety and hygiene norms. Prepare and maintain activity spaces in the Early Intervention room, Resource Centre and Vocational Unit (arranging materials, ensuring cleanliness, basic record‑keeping of resources). Assist in the use of teaching‑learning and therapy materials (toys, visual aids, communication boards, adapted equipment) as instructed by the special educator/therapist. Encourage positive behaviour, engagement and confidence among CWSN through patient, supportive interaction and consistent routines. Accompany CWSN during school events, exposure visits, sports day, cultural programmes and vocational exhibitions/fairs, ensuring safety and inclusion. Maintain cordial communication with class teachers, special educators, therapists and parents as directed by the school leadership. Attend orientation and training sessions related to disability awareness, inclusive education and vocational skills organised by the school or external agencies. Required Qualifications and Skills Minimum educational qualification: Graduation in any discipline; candidates with certification/diploma in special education, rehabilitation, arts, sports or vocational skills will be given preference. Demonstrated skill or strong interest in at least one of the following: art, dance, music, sports, theatre or vocational crafts/skills. Ability to work patiently with children, follow instructions from special educators/teachers, and maintain a positive, respectful attitude at all times. Physical ability to support children in movement and daily routines, and to manage active classroom and activity environments. Basic record‑keeping and organisation skills (e.g., maintaining simple registers for materials, attendance, or activity notes). Reporting and Supervision Reports to: Special Educator/Inclusion Coordinator and School Principal. Works in close coordination with: Class teachers, therapists, vocational trainer and other support staff. Working Conditions Full‑time role based within school premises (Early Intervention room, Resource Centre, Vocational Unit, classrooms and playground). Six working days per week; additional hours during special events may be required, with compensatory arrangements as per school policy. Key Skills and Competencies Patience, empathy and respect for children with diverse needs. Basic communication skills in Hindi; ability to follow teacher instructions and communicate with parents when required. Physical ability to assist with lifting/transfers and to be active throughout the school day (with reasonable accommodations as needed). Commitment to inclusive education, child protection and confidentiality. Industree Foundation holistically tackles the root causes of poverty by creating an ownership-based, organized, creative manufacturing ecosystem for micro-entrepreneurs. Industree works with a vision to co-create an ecosystem with farmers, artisans, and stakeholders, creating a new way of building sustainable enterprises and work culture. Further, Industree Foundation’s comprehensive approach helps maker communities assess their traditional skill base, organize them into production units, develop products that appeal to modern markets, and create consistent demand to create sustainable businesses at the lowest possible costs. Our approach has tripled the incomes of artisans in non-farm occupations by leveraging their artisanal skills and integrating them into the creative industries sector. Industree believes that if the poor have access to sustained and consistent demand for their products and services and are provided with an enabling ecosystem, they can integrate into the formal economy and lift themselves out of poverty. Over the years, we have impacted over 500,000 women across India and Africa and created market opportunities worth USD 58Mn. You can read more about Industree’s work at www.industree.org.in . Industree is collaborating with the National Rural Livelihood Mission to create livelihood opportunities for millions of women across multiple states. The NRLM-Bamboo Sub Sector program aims to work with one million women through smallholder plantation and enterprise development in each state. The project aims to support local communities in adapting to climate change through sustainable cultivation, plantation management certification, and carbon sequestration. It focuses on building long-term increases in incomes for the farmers over the period of 40-60 years. About this Position The Technical Specialist – FSC Certification will play a critical role in ensuring that bamboo plantations and processing facilities comply with FSC Forest Management (FM) and Chain of Custody (CoC) standards. This position involves overseeing audits, managing certification processes, building the capacity of operational and technical teams, and ensuring comprehensive documentation to maintain certification. The role requires active engagement with farmers, field teams, auditors, and other stakeholders to monitor compliance, address gaps, and implement corrective measures. Extensive field visits are integral to this position to ensure adherence to FSC standards and to support on-ground implementation of best practices. Roles & Responsibilities Ensure compliance with FSC standards across all plantation and processing operations, and manage annual certification, renewals, and surveillance audits with Certification Bodies. Monitor and evaluate forest management practices at the farmer and collective levels, developing strategies to maintain and improve compliance. Build the capacity of operational and technical teams to implement FSC-compliant practices on the ground. Collaborate with auditors, certification stakeholders, and relevant agencies to ensure smooth certification processes. Conduct internal FSC Forest Management (FM) and Chain of Custody (CoC) audits, inspections, and assessments in line with certification requirements. Undertake regular field visits to monitor compliance, identify gaps, and recommend corrective actions. Expected Skills & Competencies Strong understanding of FSC FM & CoC certification processes and sustainability standards Experience in audit management, compliance monitoring, and certification renewals Familiarity with forest management practices, bamboo cultivation, or agroforestry systems Excellent documentation, record-keeping, and reporting skills, ensuring compliance and audit readiness Educational Qualifications Master’s Degree in Environmental Science / Natural Resource Management (Preferred) or any relevant discipline with equivalent experience. Work Experience Minimum 5 years of experience with a strong knowledge of FSC standards, audits, and compliance processes How to apply For those interested in this role, please share your resumes along with your location, notice period/availability, and salary details at jobs@industree.org.in

title: Manager, Learning Management Operations
company: EAII Advisors (Evidence Action's technical partner in India)
description: Job Title Manager, Learning Management Operations Program: India Safe Water (ISW) Program | Evidence Action / EAII Advisors Employment Status: Regular, Full-time Position Location: Delhi (with domestic travel up to 40%) Reports to: Senior Manager, Learning Management Team, India Safe Water About the India Safe Water Team Evidence Action's India Safe Water program aims to provide safe drinking water to over 17 million people across multiple states. Through its technical partner in India, EvAc Advisors, it is delivering a major technical assistance program to help the Government of India reach millions of people with safe water, complementing the Government's effort to bring water access to every household in the country. Recent evidence highlights that water treatment may be among the most cost-effective interventions available to save young children's lives, reducing all-cause child mortality by about 25%. The In-Line Chlorination (ILC) program, based on research by a Nobel-winning economist, utilises an innovative and cost-effective solution to deliver clean water at the household level in rural settings, achieving usage rates which are 5x that of comparable interventions. EvAc Advisors ran a pilot to test the operations, cost-effectiveness and scalability of the ILC program in Rajasthan, Andhra Pradesh (AP) and Madhya Pradesh (MP), and is now scaling up in AP and other states. While implementing the scale-up, EvAc Advisors will support the Government on capacity building to effectively implement and further scale the program. About the Position We are seeking a technically strong, operationally rigorous Manager to own the ILC intervention through its full lifecycle — first establishing and validating the pilot, then driving its scale-up across new and existing geographies. This is a sequential mandate: the Manager sets up the pilot, proves the model on the ground, and subsequently leads the transition into full-scale, multi-site operations. Throughout, the role carries direct ownership of regional teams and ground operations. The ideal candidate brings deep operational and technical experience — someone who has run field operations hands-on, solved device- and system-level problems directly, and later scaled those operations into a repeatable, standardised model. 5–8 years relevant experience required. Roles and Responsibilities Operations Delivery (35%) Own day-to-day ground operations end-to-end: site setup, installation quality, O&M adherence, supply and logistics, and water-quality benchmarks. Establish the pilot's operational backbone — SOPs, workflows, escalation paths — then progressively harden and standardise these systems for scale. Run root-cause analysis on operational bottlenecks and drive continuous improvement across sites. Manage vendor performance, field logistics, and resource allocation in low-infrastructure settings. Technical Ownership (30%) Serve as the technical lead for the ILC intervention — dosing calibration, chlorine residual management, device configuration, and troubleshooting across varied field infrastructure. Own operational performance across intervention sites, including installation quality, O&M adherence, water-quality benchmarks, and real-time data validation through dashboards and raw-data review. Diagnose recurring technical and operational failures, design scalable solutions, and embed corrective protocols across teams and geographies. Collaborate with academic and technical partners, vendors, and the product team to strengthen device performance and field protocols. Team Building & Management (20%) Hire, structure, and lead new field and coordination teams - defining roles, KPIs, and reporting lines aligned to program priorities. Provide direct leadership, mentorship, and structured performance management to team members, driving accountability and a culture of transparency and learning. Run structured performance management via trackers, dashboards, and review cadences. Stakeholder Collaboration (15%) Contribute to the development of tools, frameworks, training materials, and methodologies for effective knowledge transfer and capacity building. Represent the LMT with government departments (e.g., JJM, PHED / RWSS), academic partners, and community stakeholders, championing technical and programmatic excellence. Communicate insights, risks, and recommendations to ISW leadership in a timely and structured manner. Requirements Essential Bachelor's degree in Engineering (Civil, Mechanical, Chemical, or Environmental) or a closely related technical discipline. Minimum of 5–8 years of experience in technically complex program delivery, with demonstrable, including hands-on field operations and a subsequent scale-up. Proven experience hiring, structuring, and leading teams, ideally across dispersed geographies in rural or resource-limited settings. Strong ability to use data for decision-making, protocol design, and continuous improvement. Excellent spoken and written English, with the ability to synthesise information and produce high-quality documents to tight deadlines. Willingness to travel up to 40% of the time domestically. Desirable Master's degree in Engineering, Management, or a related discipline. Experience running large, multi-site field operations, ideally having taken an operation from pilot through to scale-up. Exceptional ability to work with minimal supervision while proactively surfacing progress and bottlenecks to leadership. What Success Looks Like The pilot is set up and running as a stable, well-documented operation — installations meet quality standards, O&M routines run reliably, and water-quality benchmarks (chlorine residual, dosing accuracy) are consistently met. Robust operational foundations — SOPs, installation and O&M workflows, and escalation mechanisms — are established and consistently followed in every new site. The Manager develops a strong working grasp of the ILC device and its engineering logic — how it functions, common failure points, and what does and does not work in the field — enabling sound, timely technical judgment without dependence on specialists for every decision. High-performing field and coordination teams are hired, structured, and retained, with defined roles, KPIs, and low attrition in resource-limited settings. Skills & Competencies Technical aptitude and a strong appetite to absorb engineering and device-level knowledge — while not necessarily an engineer by training, the person understands how the ILC device works, why it fails, and what does and does not work in practice, and can engage credibly with technical teams. Strong project management, with the ability to run multiple workstreams and priorities simultaneously across dispersed geographies. Data-driven decision-making, with comfort synthesizing dashboards and raw field data into protocol design and continuous improvement. People leadership and coaching, with a track record of hiring, structuring, and developing high-performing teams in rural or resource-limited settings. How to apply To apply, please click here: Manager, Learning Management Operations (EAII Advisors)

title: Field Supervisor
description: Designation Field Supervisor Location Jharkhand No. of Vacancies 3 Project Background: The Global Alliance for Viksit Bharat (GAVB) is a landmark social development initiative designed to uplift 200 million Indians living in multidimensional poverty. With a transformative investment, GAVB concentrates efforts on five priority states—Jharkhand, Assam, Chhattisgarh, Odisha, and Bihar (JACOB states)—which are disproportionately impacted by acute poverty. Health and Education account for 67% of the Multi-dimensional Poverty Index (MDPI). GAVB works closely with state governments to strengthen public health systems, improve service delivery, and enhance community wellbeing. The Communicable Disease (CD) portfolio specifically addresses Tuberculosis (TB) and Malaria—two diseases that disproportionately affect vulnerable populations including tribal communities, urban poor, and migrant workers. GAVB's approach leverages Digitization, Decentralization, Leadership & Institutions, and Inclusion to enhance health service delivery. Domain expertise with proven solutions lays the foundation for introduction, progression, and gradual integration of innovations into government public health systems. As states prepare to accelerate efforts as a part of GAVB, there is a need to develop a nuanced understanding of the current status of service delivery systems, implementation readiness, and context-specific challenges before introducing new interventions. In this regard, an Immersive Diagnostic Deep Dive (IDD) is planned. This is a recruitment advertisement for field supervisor this IDD exercise. The Field Supervisor will undertake the quality checks and supervision of the data collection, providing hand holding support to the team (field investigators) through QAQC process (Spot-check, back-check and audio-check) and ensuring the data collection timely in her/his assigned district/blocks. S/he will ensure complete adherence to protocol, and high efficiency and quality of data collection. They will work in close coordination with the State RMLE team (PD/ SPL/PL/Sr Analyst) and accountable for the overall success of the RMLE data collection. Based on the need they will also collect data in other than the assigned districts. Roles and Responsibilities To be thorough with the implementation protocol of the study and to ensure its adherence by the deployed Field investigators To maintain data sanctity by conducting rigorous and time-bound back-checks, spot-checks and Audio checks of the data collected by the Field Investigators To monitor field investigators, maintain their daily output. Ensure zero tolerance in case of data fudging. To provide hand-holding support to FI’s as and when needed. To conduct primary data collection as and when required. To support in maintenance of logistics and field movement planning. To prepare and share consolidated reports on the quality of data collection. Conduct 10% to 15% quality checks (Spot, back and audio checks) of collected data. Minimum Qualification : Bachelor's degree or post-graduation in any discipline with two/three years of relevant work experience in public health programs. Excellent communication skills in Hindi and local dialects of Jharkhand. Experience with large scale household survey data collection in public health (Household survey, CMWRA, Facility surveys) Experience of working in any Maternal and Child Health program (or, at least any Public Health Program) Strong understanding of Public Health Program (including ICDS) and exposure to different terminologies used in Maternal and Child Health Programs Experienced in managing teams in any project, being a supervisor or monitor for minimum one year Preferred: Excellent communication skills in Hindi and other local dialects (Santahli, Mundari, Khortha and Ho) and functional understanding of English is also required. Understanding of cultural sensitivities of Jharkhand. Proven experience in conducting large-scale household, family planning, or community-level surveys. Strong understanding of Public Health Program (including ICDS) and exposure to different terminologies used in Maternal and Child Health Programs. He must have his own android phone. Must have two-wheelers with a valid driving license. title: Director of Alumni Leadership, Asia Pacific
description: About Teach for India Teach For India is a nationwide movement of leaders dedicated to providing an excellent education for all children. These include both Fellows, who commit two years to teaching low-income & under-resourced classrooms, as well as Staff teams, who bolster these efforts through strategic support & organizational direction. Position Summary This role is part of Teach for All’s Global Alumni Leadership Team, with counterparts in other regions to spread learning and innovation across regions. The role reports to the Head of Alumni Leadership but works in very close -daily- collaboration with colleagues in Teach for All’s Asia Pacific regional team and our global Collective Learning & Consulting team. Key Responsibilities Network Partner Support There are currently 20 organizations that Teach for All supports across the Asia Pacific region. Each organization is developing their alumni leaders at the local level. To support their efforts, you will: Collaborate with Teach For All’s Asia Pacific regional team and Functional Area specialists to diagnose and constantly re-evaluate the needs and strengths of partners to determine and deliver the most appropriate support strategies and capture and share innovations and learnings. Establish strong, trust-based relationships with Heads of Program and Heads of Alumni in Asia Pacific, engaging regularly to understand their unique challenges, successes, and areas of growth. Work in close partnership with specialists across and beyond Teach For All to remain at the forefront of the latest network knowledge and insights about developing collective leadership through the recruitment, selection, placement and training of leaders, contributing new insights as you come across them, and developing shared learning experiences. Manage alumni data and share insights (based on your diagnosis of a partners’ needs and priorities) through various mediums including facilitating learning experiences, workshops, newsletters and online platforms, driving learning and engagement amongst Heads of Alumni and Heads of Program. Manage a robust learning community between Heads of Alumni in Asia Pacific which facilitates peer learning, information exchange, peer support, collaboration between them to accelerate their local efforts. Provide personalized coaching and consulting to Heads of Alumni and other Senior Leaders, leveraging your expertise to address specific challenges and enhance the effectiveness of their alumni impact strategies. Influence Chief Program Officers and network partner CEOs, in close partnership with the regional team, to build momentum for alumni support outside of the Head of Alumni role and collaborate with others to execute high quality cross-functional support and learning across many senior stakeholders to ensure alumni strategy and support is a priority for network partners in the region. Develop Alumni Leaders There are currently ~13,000 alumni leaders in the Asia Pacific region who have successfully completed their two years as a participant in one of the Teach For All network partners across the region and are now continuing to work as leaders in education and across additional sectors. To support their collective growth, learning and impact as leaders across the region, you will: Proactively build strong, credible relationships with alumni leaders to understand their unique challenges, successes, and areas of growth. You will be the Teach For All “point person” for alumni to field their requests and ideas, and the ‘go-to’ for Teach for All staff with questions about alumni in the region. Partner with the Asia Pacific regional team, network CEOs and Heads of Alumni to create and execute programs to accelerate alumni leadership and connectivity at the regional level such as the Asia Pacific Alumni Summit, Policy Fellowships and School Leader development programs. Coordinate small groups of alumni volunteers including our Network Connectors to best leverage their energy and skills towards our goals. Manage a vibrant online community of alumni on WhatsApp to foster their connectivity, learning and to share opportunities for leadership development. Manage applications from the Asia Pacific region to Teach for All’s Communities & Connections Fund to enable alumni to self-organize regional virtual and in-person learning exchanges. Capture and share stories of alumni leadership and impact to inspire and motivate others and demonstrate progress in the region Qualifications Prior experience and a strong track record of impact as an alumni and/or senior leader from within the Teach for All network in the Asia Pacific region 8+ years of relevant working experience with a credible background in leadership, leadership development, systems change, and/or network building Passion and experience in growing the leadership capacities of others through training and coaching Exceptional communication skills capable of distilling complex ideas and data into clear, actionable insights for diverse audiences Proven ability to build strong, credible relationships with multiple stakeholders to understand their goals and motivations to support collaboration while working virtually and remotely Exceptional strategic thinking abilities with proven track record of diagnosing and solving complex problems, exercising strong judgment and working with ambiguity Ability to work collaboratively and flexibly with colleagues globally, including a high volume of virtual engagement (i.e., conference calls, virtual collaboration tools) Superior project management skills; a self-starter with the ability to manage multiple streams of work, use strong judgment to independently determine actions and prioritize tasks, and work effectively in a dynamic, globally dispersed team environment Experience and ability to design and execute powerful remote and in-person learning experiences (events, workshops, etc.) Strong orientation towards diversity, inclusivity and equity with heightened levels of self-awareness, cross cultural competence and humility, and ability to adapt approach and communications styles accordingly Ability to influence and motivate others outside of direct team relationships Must be able to work fluently in English Additional desirable skills Prior experience as a coach or consultant or launching/ leading own venture Experience managing virtual peer learning communities and building strong peer networks Experience managing and mobilizing volunteers How to apply For more information, please check the link: Director of Alumni Leadership, Asia Pacific

title: Manager - Program Strategy & Operations
description: About SOL'S ARC Sol’s ARC is a unique organization that does innovative educational research to build inclusive pedagogy in both mainstream and special schools to ensure that every child can learn. Sol’s ARC has a distinctive perspective on special education where we look at the beneficiaries from two different lenses- one children who have special needs due to socio economic conditions and the other due to disabilities. Our approach is based on special education principles to ensure that pedagogy is inclusive and can address diverse educational needs across the classroom regardless of why the learning gap e THE ROLE This is a mid-to-senior role for someone who is good at turning plans into action. You will manage the day-to-day delivery of Sol's ARC's programmes, keep teams on track, handle donor reporting, and ensure the Director of program and Strategy has everything she needs to lead externally. This is a hands-on role — you will be expected to solve problems, coordinate teams across locations, and be accountable for outcomes. It needs to travel to field locations. HOW YOU'LL SPEND YOUR TIME 50% Programme planning and operations 20% Monitoring, reporting and donor compliance 15% Team coordination and capacity building 15% Stakeholder liaison and internal alignment WHAT YOU'LL DO Track work plans and operations per program Track all Sol's ARC programmes — inclusive education, skilling, livelihoods — are running on time and within budget. Build work plans, activity calendars and milestone trackers for each programme. Review progresses every week with state and field teams. Travel every quarter for one week to engagement and understand ground realities Track programme budgets with the Finance team. Make sure expenses match the donor agreement heads. Prepare utilization certificates on time. Manage programme changes, scale-ups and closures as needed. Reporting and donor compliance Build a reporting system that gives accurate and timely data to donors, government partners and the leadership team. Write programme progress reports and review financial reports. Make sure all reports match agreed milestones and indicators. Work with the M&E team to track what has been done and what outcomes have been achieved. Keep all programme documents — SOPs, field protocols, frameworks — organized and up to date. Flag risks and problems to the Director early, with your suggested solutions. Team coordination and capacity building Coordinate with programme, M&E, finance, HR and communications teams to keep delivery on track. Directly support state-level coordinators and team leads — help them plan, execute and report. Run regular team meetings and review sessions. Help new programme staff settle into their roles. Stakeholder liaison and internal alignment Be the main point of contact for government departments and implementation partners on day-to-day programme matters. Prepare briefing notes, updates and presentation materials for the Director to use in meetings with government, donors and the Board. Represent Sol's ARC in partner coordination meetings when required. Qualifications and experience Master’s degree in social work, Development Studies, Public Policy, MBA or a related field. Strong practical experience will be considered in place of qualifications. 4–5 years of experience in programme operations or project management, with at least 2 years managing multi-location, multi-donor programmes in a nonprofit or development sector organization. Experience managing field teams across multiple states or districts. Strong track record of donor reporting, MoU compliance and milestone-based accountability. Experience working with government bodies (education, social justice, skill development) is an advantage. Familiarity with the RPwD Act, NEP 2020 or NIPUN Bharat is preferred. Skills Strong planning and organizational skills — can manage multiple workstreams without losing track of detail. Clear written communication — can write donor reports and programme briefs independently. Comfortable working with MIS systems, dashboards and outcome data. Works well with others but can drive accountability and make decisions when needed. Takes ownership — does not wait to be told; anticipates problems and resolves them. What makes an exceptional candidate All programmes delivered on time, within budget, and with no surprises at the end of a reporting period. The Director spends her time on strategy and external engagement — not chasing programme updates. Field teams feel supported, clear on their targets, and accountable. Donors receive accurate, insightful reports that reflect real programme progress. WHAT WE OFFER Salary as per Sol's ARC pay scale, based on your experience. Travel reimbursement for all programme-related travel. Outcomes-based flexible work — targets are clear; how you plan your day is up to you. Training and support from the programme team when you join. How to apply For more information, please check the link: Manager - Program Strategy & Operations

title: Programme Mentor Early Years
description: About Vipla Foundation Vipla Foundation is a non-profit organization established in 1988, working in the areas of early childhood care and education, health, nutrition, women’s empowerment, and vocational training. The organization partners with government bodies and communities to strengthen systems for children’s development, particularly in underserved urban contexts. It has been awarded "Best NGO in INDIA – 2011” by the Indian NGO Awards which is a joint venture between the Resource Alliance and The Rockefeller Foundation & also by the Institute of Public Enterprise. Save The Children India is now known as Vipla Foundation. A new name. A renewed commitment to ensure that nothing stops the children of India from learning, growing and flourishing. At our core lies the intention to ensure that nothing stops the children of India from learning, growing and flourishing. About the Programme Capacity building of Anganwadi Sevikas in Uran the Uran Anganwadi Project will aim to strengthen Anganwadi centers as safe, engaging, and developmentally appropriate early learning spaces through structured mentoring and capacity building. The programme will focus on building the capacities of 123 Anganwadi Sevikas in Uran through planned training and continuous on-site mentoring to improve classroom practices, learning environments, and teacher–child interactions. Mentors support Anganwadi workers in applying training into daily practice, using simple monitoring tools to track quality and children’s progress. The project also includes ongoing, age-appropriate assessments to understand children’s learning needs, support their overall development, and ensure a smooth transition to formal schooling in an inclusive and supportive early learning environment. Key Roles & Responsibilities Mentor and support approximately 25 assigned Anganwadi Sevikas through regular field visits. Plan and facilitate trainings, refresher sessions, and other capacity-building activities for Anganwadi workers. Observe teacher–child interactions, classroom management, teaching practices, and learning environments and provide constructive feedback. Support Anganwadi Sevikas in applying training inputs and best practices in them day-to-day classroom practices. Maintain accurate and timely documentation of mentoring visits, programme activities, observations, and progress. Regularly use the digital monitoring and evaluation application to record, review, and analyze programme data for continuous improvement. Skills & Competencies Strong understanding of early childhood education and development (ages 3–6) Ability to mentor adults using supportive, non-judgmental approaches Comfort with mobile-based applications and basic data analysis Good observation, documentation, and feedback skills Clear communication in Hindi and/or Marathi; working knowledge of English Ability to manage multiple centers and field schedules independently Willingness to travel extensively within Navi Mumbai Qualify cations & Experience Diploma or Degree in Early Childhood Education, Human Development, Social Work, or related fields Minimum 1 year of experience in preschool teaching, teacher training, or academic mentoring (preferred) Experience working with Anganwadi systems or government programmes is an advantage Other Expectations High levels of accountability, punctuality, and professional conduct Openness to learning and adapting to programme and digitization requirements Commitment to child-centered, inclusive, and developmentally appropriate practices How to apply For more information, please check the link: Programme Mentor Early Years

title: Finance Associate
description: About Myna Mahila Foundation Myna Mahila Foundation is a women’s health and livelihoods organisation working at scale across India. Founded in Mumbai, Myna operates across Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, and Haryana, with active partnerships across state governments, multilateral funders, and corporate philanthropies. Myna’s work spans menstrual health, reproductive and sexual health, livelihoods generation for low-income women, and a digital health worker programme (Bolo) that has reached over 16,000 women in its first year. The organisation is in a moment of significant geographic expansion. We implement a Women’s Agency Program, which empowers women in urban poor communities by increasing their health autonomy and economic independence. This program operates through local Women’s Empowerment Hubs — both physical centers and digital platforms — providing accessible spaces for comprehensive health education, healthcare services, and skill-building economic opportunities. Job Summary The Finance Associate is responsible for supporting the organization's financial operations by maintaining accurate accounting records, processing financial transactions, ensuring compliance with statutory requirements, assisting in audits, and providing administrative support. The role requires strong accounting knowledge, attention to detail, and the ability to coordinate effectively with internal teams and external stakeholders. Ensure financial documents are organized, updated, and readily available for audits and reviews. 5.Stakeholder Coordination Coordinate with banks, auditors, vendors, and service providers as required. Liaise with internal teams to ensure timely submission of financial information and expense reports. 6.Administrative Support Support day-to-day administrative activities related to finance and office operations. Perform additional finance, accounting, and administrative tasks assigned by the Finance Manager. Qualifications Bachelor's degree in Commerce, Accounting, Finance, or a related discipline. 2–4 years of experience in accounting and finance operations. Proficiency in Tally ERP 9 and Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel. Working knowledge of GST, TDS, Income Tax, and audit processes. Skills & Competencies Strong accounting and bookkeeping skills. Good analytical and problem-solving abilities. Attention to detail and high level of accuracy. Strong organizational and documentation skills. Effective communication and coordination abilities. Ability to manage multiple priorities and meet deadlines. Integrity, confidentiality, and professionalism. Preferred Qualifications Experience working with NGOs, trusts, societies, or non-profit organizations. Familiarity with FCRA regulations and reporting requirements. Experience in financial reporting, compliance, and audit coordination. How to apply Application Process Please send your resume along with a cover letter to work@mynafoundation.com.

title: Communications Officer
description: About India Foundation for the Arts India Foundation for the Arts (IFA) is an independent, nationwide, not-for-profit organization that makes grants and implements projects across research, practice and education in the arts and culture in India, since 1995. We have supported over 950 projects disbursing over Rs 41 crore across the country. The outcomes of these projects—as books, films, performances, exhibitions, games, websites, and archival materials—have been circulating in the public domain through showcases, presentations, seminars, screenings, lecture demonstrations, and festivals, helping widen access and encouraging broader participation in the arts. JOB DESCRIPTION We are looking for a Communications Officer who will be responsible for all communication tasks related to the organization, is excited about creating engaging communication to spread the word about the work IFA does, someone who can garner support for the arts through evocative writing and strategic communication plans and can drive Social Media outreach. The selected candidate will be part of the Communications and Outreach team and will report to Lead: Communications and Outreach. RESPONSIBILITIES Writing Write and edit crisp, concise, and accessible communication material, aimed at internal and external audiences, for print, social media, website, and e-mailers, and ensure that institutional documents are up to date. This would include but isn’t limited to Requests for Proposals, Project Showcases, Date with the Archive, Plans and Quarterly Reviews, press notes, Brochures, Festival and Conference documents, Annual Reports, Calendars, Newsletters, Website. title: Suraksha Coordinator – Jhargram
description: JOB DESCRIPTION Suraksha Coordinator – Jhargram About Mukti Mukti is a development organisation dedicated to advancing the well-being, education and empowerment of children, young people and underserved communities. Through its work with schools and communities, Mukti strives to foster safe, inclusive and enabling environments where children can learn, grow and realise their potential. Safeguarding is integral to Mukti’s organisational ethos. The organisation has established robust Child Safeguarding and POSH (Prevention of Sexual Harassment) Policies and is committed to maintaining the highest standards of safety, dignity, inclusion, professional integrity and accountability across all its programmes and engagements. About Suraksha Songlap Suraksha Songlap is a school-based initiative designed to strengthen child safety, gender sensitivity, awareness and safeguarding practices among adolescents, teachers, facilitators and the wider school community. The programme is being implemented in three project schools in Jhargram: Ranarani, Banpukhuria and Manikpara . Position Designation: Suraksha Coordinator Location: Jhargram, West Bengal Project: Suraksha Songlap Reporting to: Suraksha Programme Manager Remuneration: ₹12,000 per month + TA on actual basis Travel: Frequent travel between the three project schools will be an integral part of the role. Key Purpose of the Role: The Suraksha Coordinator will be responsible for the effective field-level implementation, coordination, monitoring and documentation of the Suraksha Songlap programme across the three project schools. The Coordinator will work under the continuous guidance and supervision of the Suraksha Programme Manager , receive appropriate programme-related training, and subsequently provide on-site support and training to the facilitators implementing Suraksha activities in the schools. The position requires a proactive, responsible and field-oriented individual who can build positive relationships with schools, work closely with facilitators and local stakeholders, observe programme implementation closely, and ensure that activities are completed effectively and documented appropriately. Key Responsibilities 1. Facilitator Training and Support ● Receive continuous guidance, mentoring and appropriate training from the Suraksha Programme Manager. ● Conduct on-site training, orientation and handholding support for facilitators in the three project schools. ● Regularly interact with facilitators to understand implementation challenges and provide support within the scope of the programme. ● Identify training and capacity-building needs and communicate these to the Suraksha Programme Manager. ● Ensure that facilitators understand the objectives, methodology and safeguarding principles of the Suraksha programme. 2. School Coordination and Relationship Building ● Maintain regular and professional communication with the three project schools— Ranarani, Banpukhuria and Manikpara . ● With the support of the local Field Coordinator, develop and maintain a positive working relationship with the concerned government school authorities, teachers and other relevant stakeholders. ● Coordinate with schools to facilitate smooth implementation of programme activities. ● Communicate the programme schedule and requirements to the concerned school personnel in a timely manner. 3. Programme Planning and Implementation ● Prepare and maintain a programme calendar in consultation with the Suraksha Programme Manager and the respective schools. ● Plan frequent field visits and travel between the three project schools, keeping the Suraksha Programme Manager informed and obtaining necessary guidance. ● Be personally present during Suraksha-related activities wherever required to ensure smooth and effective implementation. ● Observe programme sessions and activities closely and provide constructive feedback to facilitators. ● Ensure that planned activities are implemented according to the programme framework, timelines and quality standards. ● Identify field-level challenges and escalate them promptly to the Suraksha Programme Manager. 4. Monitoring, Observation and Documentation ● Regularly monitor programme implementation across all three schools. ● Document key observations, participation, progress, challenges, outcomes and significant developments. ● Maintain appropriate records, reports, photographs and other programme documentation as required. ● Support the Suraksha Programme Manager in compiling periodic programme updates, progress reports and outcome documentation. ● Ensure that programme records are accurate, timely and properly maintained. 5. Coordination with Mukti Team ● Work collaboratively with the Suraksha Programme Manager, MSS Coordinators, HR team and other relevant Mukti personnel . ● Participate in online meetings, review meetings and programme discussions as required. ● Maintain timely communication with the concerned team members regarding field activities, progress, challenges and emerging concerns. ● Follow Mukti's organisational policies, procedures and professional standards at all times. 6. Child Safeguarding and Gender ● Demonstrate a clear understanding of child safeguarding, child rights, gender equality, adolescent well-being and prevention of abuse and exploitation . ● Ensure that all programme activities are conducted in a safe, respectful, inclusive and child-sensitive manner. ● Familiarity with child protection mechanisms, safeguarding principles, gender-related programmes or adolescent-focused interventions will be considered a strong advantage. ● Strictly adhere to Mukti's Child Safeguarding Policy and POSH Policy and immediately report any safeguarding concern through the appropriate organisational channels. Required Qualifications and Competencies Essential ● The candidate must be a resident of Jhargram district. ● Minimum Graduate degree from a recognised institution. ● A certificate, diploma or degree or work experience in Child Protection, Child Rights, Social Work, Gender Studies, Development Studies or a related discipline will be highly preferred. ● Basic computer literacy with the ability to: prepare and maintain documents and reports; use email effectively; participate in online meetings; maintain basic digital records and documentation. ● Ability to understand and communicate in simple English , both verbally and in writing. ● Good communication and interpersonal skills. ● Willingness and ability to undertake frequent field travel between the three project schools in Jhargram. ● Ability to work independently in the field while remaining closely connected with the Programme Manager and the wider Mukti team. Desirable ● Prior experience working with children, adolescents, schools, child protection, gender, safeguarding or community-based programmes . ● Formal training or certification in child safeguarding, child rights, gender or related areas. ● Experience of working with government schools or community-based organisations. ● Ability to facilitate group sessions, training or orientation programmes. ● Sensitivity, maturity and confidence in handling child- and gender-related issues. Key Personal Attributes The ideal candidate should be: ● Child-sensitive, empathetic and responsible ● Proactive and willing to work extensively in the field ● A good listener and communicator ● Organised and attentive to documentation ● Comfortable working with school authorities, teachers and community stakeholders ● Open to learning and receiving continuous supervision and feedback ● Able to maintain confidentiality and professional boundaries ● Committed to safeguarding, gender equality and creating safe spaces for children and adolescents Nature of the Role This is a field-intensive coordination role requiring regular movement between the three project schools. The Coordinator is expected not merely to coordinate activities remotely , but to remain physically present, observe implementation, support facilitators, build school relationships, identify challenges and document programme outcomes . The role offers an opportunity to contribute directly to creating safer, more inclusive and gender-sensitive school environments for children and adolescents in Jhargram. Remuneration: ₹12,000 per month + TA on actual basis. How to apply Please share your updated CV mentioning the post applied for to careers@muktiweb.org

Work Experience: Training/teaching experience in schools. Good program knowledge and relevant training experience in life skills/mental health wellness curriculum. Good data analysis skills with program planning and design, monitoring and evaluation frameworks and techniques. Good analytical and numeracy skills. Ability to travel extensively. description: About YosAid Innovation Foundation YosAid Innovation Foundation improves outcomes and strengthens health systems in India by promoting innovative healthcare practices and skills among patients and their families. YosAid Innovation Foundation envisions a paradigm shift in healthcare delivery, where family caregivers of patients are engaged and supported in caring for their loved ones. This mobile phone-based service provides families with a platform to interact with health and health service-related questions in their regional languages to which a dedicated team of nurses and doctors respond. Expansion of these programs in other areas of Nutrition, Nephrology & Oncology is underway in multiple Indian states. MO’s primary responsibility will be to support seamless interactions between patients/caregivers, nursing staff and consultant physicians, ensuring the patients receive evidence based high - quality health information and guidance throughout their healthcare journey. This is not a tele-medicine service but a tele-health programme that supports patients and /or caregivers with an understanding of relevant health conditions. We focus on behavior change rather than just prescribing medication. The role of an MO role will also involve preparing data-based reports to be shared with the internal medical team on the queries asked on the platform, training of the nurses on key medical topics, facilitating tele training and supporting the team with messaging interventions. The role of the MO is to support service improvement of the program by offering inputs on quality, accuracy and relevance of the content. Ensure prompt response when a query is escalated by the in-house two-way response team. Our in-house two-way response team of nurses are the first responders to all questions raised by the users. Some of our questions require a more experienced clinician’s intervention and will be shared with doctors. The expected response time once the questions are shared is 30 min -1 hour. In-case of an emergency question, the response time must be within 5 minutes. Our telehealth service does not share information on diagnosis or prescribe medication but is confined to tele-health education and health promotion. This is where you come in! To ensure that all the relevant questions are escalated and responded to promptly, compassionately, with accurate medication information. Ensure prompt response when a question is escalated by the in-house clinical team. Your role will need you to contribute to the growing landscape of digital health with a medical lens to improve the service and make it more patient - centered.
