title: Social Worker
description: About iProbono India iProbono India brings together the legal expertise of its carefully curated community of panel and network lawyers, ground-level insights of its grassroots partners, and the ethos of social action litigation to advance justice and equality in India. We focus our efforts on child rights, housing justice, and strengthening civil society. Role We are looking for a Social Worker for our Comprehensive Care Team in Delhi – a team member who will provide wraparound support to the individuals and communities we represent. The social worker will primarily be responsible for providing direct support to survivors of child sexual abuse and their families. Additionally, the social worker will also work with children (alleged to be) in conflict with law in planning interventions for their rehabilitation. The role entails liaisoning with and reporting to the Child Welfare Committees (CWC), Juvenile Justice Board, Child Care Institutions and other agencies. The social worker may also be required to support other verticals as and when required. Responsibilities The social worker will be performing the duties of a ‘support person’ in accordance with the POCSO Rules, 2020. They must: Provide direct support to children in need of care and protection and their families. Conduct home visits and identify psychosocial needs requiring immediate attention. Work with the concerned stakeholders to help children receive interim and final victim compensation according to the government schemes. Proactively liaison with government authorities, especially CWC members, District Child Protection Unit, Delhi State Legal Services Authority, police officials, and counsels. Send regular updates to the CWC, as mandated. Assist children and families for court hearings, attend court hearings and support clients through legal processes wherever required. Work closely with panel lawyers on cases where iProbono India is providing legal representation. Assist child survivors at the police station and during medical procedures, wherever required. Ensure compliance with the provisions of applicable laws and rules applicable to support persons, including provisions of the POCSO Act and Rules, Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015 etc. Further, the social worker must be thorough with social work methods for planning interventions to support the rehabilitation of children (alleged to be) in conflict with law. The status reports of such interventions will be submitted before the Juvenile Justice Board/Probation Officer. Additional Responsibilities Working closely with the entire India Programs Team to ensure that all clients receive holistic, wraparound support. Consistent, thorough and timely documentation of client case information in the case management system. Participating in training and capacity building sessions for beneficiaries, panel lawyers, partner organizations etc., as required. Working with partner NGOs, government agencies and field workers to provide support to clients in the Juvenile Justice/Criminal Justice verticals. Skills and Experience (as per the guidelines of the Department of Women & Child Development, Delhi) Master’s degree in social work with at least 1 year of relevant experience or a bachelor’s degree in social work with a minimum of three years’ experience in child education and development or child protection. Individuals having experience of working in registered children’s homes or shelter homes responsible for the care and custody of children may also apply. Demonstrated knowledge of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012, the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015, and the child protection system is essential. Experience in providing psychosocial support, case management, child safeguarding, or rehabilitation services for children in vulnerable situations. Strong interpersonal, and communication skills, with the ability to engage sensitively with children, families, government stakeholders, and partner organizations. Ability to prepare case records, maintain confidentiality, and coordinate with District Child Protection Units, Special Courts, Child Welfare Committees, and other relevant stakeholders. Proficiency in spoken and written English, Hindi, and/or the local language of the district is desirable. Basic computer proficiency, including documentation, reporting, and use of Microsoft Office applications. How to apply For more information, please check the link: Social Worker

title: State Program Officer
company: EAII Advisors (Evidence Action's technical partner in India)
description: Job Title: State Program Officer Organization: EAII Advisors, Evidence Action’s technical partner in India Location: Vijayawada, Andhra Pradesh Travel: Approximately 50% in-state travel About EAII EAII Advisors, Evidence Action’s technical partner in India, supports state governments in delivering evidence-based public health programs, including safe drinking water initiatives and school and Anganwadi-based National Deworming Day and iron and folic acid supplementation. Operating across 10 states, EAII Advisors provides technical assistance to ministries of health, education, water, and women and child development, reducing health burdens in impoverished communities and improving the long-term wellbeing of children and families. About Evidence Action At Evidence Action, we deliver data-driven interventions that transform lives at an unprecedented scale. We identify neglected global health issues and deploy proven solutions, forging healthier futures for generations. Our model operationalizes leading academic research (including from Nobel-winning economists). We measure progress and outcomes at every stage to ensure we’re making a real impact for people living in poverty and suffering from preventable or treatable health issues. Operating across 11 countries, our team of 900+ has reached over 500 million people, working closely with governments to scale these interventions. Our Deworm the World program has delivered over 2 billion treatments, significantly reducing worm prevalence and generating more than $23 billion in lifetime productivity gains. Through Safe Water Now, we’ve saved the lives of over 15,000 children. Our Accelerator explores untapped opportunities in global health, testing low-cost interventions with the greatest potential to save and improve lives. At Evidence Action, your colleagues are your greatest asset. You'll partner with high-caliber colleagues in an environment blending innovation, autonomy, and teamwork. Our team excels in disruptive thinking and believes in rolling up our sleeves to get things done. If you're looking to work flexibly and with purpose, join a team that delivers measurable change for millions. The Role The State Program Officer will report to the State Program Lead and be based at Vijayawada, Andhra Pradesh. The SPO will help adapt and execute Evidence Action’s technical assistance approach for Iron and Folic Acid (IFA) supplementation under Anaemia Mukt Bharat in Andhra Pradesh, working closely with NHM – Andhra Pradesh/DoHFW, Department of Education, WCD/ICDS, and other partners. The role focuses on high-quality program planning, budget inclusion, supply-chain enablement to the last mile, training cascades, monitoring and coverage validation, and data-driven advocacy. The position involves collaboration with Evidence Action’s MLE, Finance/Procurement, and National Office teams and requires approximately 50% in-state travel. Responsibilities Policy Advocacy Ensure IFA activities are well planned and adequately budgeted in State PIPs/RoPs, including for pilots/scale-ups. Prepare brief, actionable advocacy notes using field data and evidence; support SPL in state-level decision forums to drive corrective actions across TA areas. Support GoAP to convene regular review meetings (Health, Education, WCD/ICDS) with clear agendas, data packs, minutes, and action trackers. Coordinate with the Health/NHM IEC cell and Education/WCD counterparts to refresh IFA IEC/BCC content and integrate IFA/WIFS in school platforms; facilitate timely circulars, guidelines, and orders. Engage with allied state platforms and partner agencies to strengthen community mobilisation and dissemination. Program Design & Development Coordinate with the National Office and state stakeholders to align state plans with national guidance and GoAP priorities to improve quality and effectiveness. Prepare the state IFA implementation plan with SPL/NO; define milestones, roles, and risk mitigations. Support M&E process design and tool development with the MLE team; ensure data flows enable timely supervision and course correction. Provide inputs on community mobilisation approaches; identify need-based IEC and social-media materials. Contribute to state program budgets and support training cascades (design, materials, delivery quality, reach). Program Management With the SPL, develop/manage workplans and timelines; track deliverables for internal/external needs; keep SPL updated on progress and risks. Guide and support Regional Coordinators (RCs) for effective field implementation and issue resolution. Develop guidelines, trackers, and tools (supply, coverage, training, supervision, reporting) for implementation and monitoring. Undertake field visits to provide technical support, supervise activities, and liaise with district officials. Work with SPC-MLE to qualitatively analyze monitoring data and provide feedback to field teams for improved coverage validation (“any” and “full” coverage). Coordinate with government procurement/logistics counterparts (e.g., state logistics MIS/medical services corp.) to strengthen indenting, allocation, and last-mile distribution. Knowledge Management Prepare program briefs, process documentation, case studies, and best-practice notes; facilitate dissemination with stakeholders. Engage with stakeholders alongside SPL to share findings and lessons from implementation. Maintain up-to-date program documentation and adhere to KM/file-storage/access guidelines. Requirements Essentials Postgraduate degree in public health, nutrition, health management, Social work or related disciplines. 9–10 years’ experience in the development sector, preferably delivering technical/advisory support to the Government. Experience collaborating with the Government on maternal, child health, and nutrition programs. At least 3 years of experience working with Government departments in Andhra Pradesh. Demonstrated experience in supporting and managing teams. Strong knowledge of public-sector health systems and programs; good understanding of public-health and socio-economic issues in Andhra Pradesh. Ability to synthesize information clearly and produce high-quality documents to tight deadlines. Excellent communication, presentation, and documentation skills in English; working proficiency in Telugu required. Proficient with Microsoft Office and Google applications. Ability to work with minimal supervision while proactively communicating progress, risks, and support needs. Willingness to travel up to 50% of the time within the state. Desirable Familiarity with Andhra Pradesh’s socio-cultural context and administrative processes. Action-oriented, flexible, and entrepreneurial problem-solver with strong prioritization across multiple deadlines. Highly motivated to achieve exceptional quality; able to manage multiple tasks simultaneously. Ability to communicate effectively across stakeholder levels. Strong interest in the development sector and working in diverse, mission-driven teams. Position Location This role will be based in Vijayawada, Andhra Pradesh. Applicants must be legally authorized to work in India. EAII is unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of employment visas at this time. Benefits include: Comprehensive health insurance with IPD and OPD provisions Life and Accidental insurance PF, ESIC and Gratuity as per statutory requirements Mental and physical well-being benefits Learning and Development benefit Generous leave Avenues for engagement and recognition Compensation Competitive and commensurate with the individual's credentials, experience, and previous pay scale. All contracting arrangements will be made through EAII Advisors Private Limited. EAII is an equal opportunity employer. Employment at EAII is based solely on an individual's merit and qualifications directly related to professional competence. EAII does not discriminate against any employee or applicant because of race, caste, creed, colour, religion, gender, origin, disability, marital status, or any other basis protected by law. title: CASE MANAGER
description: SENIOR CASE MANAGER Base Location: Mumbai Education: Graduate or Postgraduate degree in Social Work Language requirement: English, Hindi required & Marathi optional Background: RATI (Rights. Action. Technology. Inclusion.) Foundation, is a Mumbai-based organisation, that works to address gender based violence against women and children in both online and offline spaces by supporting survivors and families until they thrive again. We address the issue of gender-based violence through three interconnected pillars: immediate response, long-term survivor recovery and systemic reform. Our helpline, Meri Trustline, is India’s trusted support service for online abuse. Beyond this, through our Socio Legal Interventions we provide on-ground legal representation, counseling and social support to children and women survivors of gender violence. What sets RATI apart is our multidisciplinary team that has the ability to work across multiple vulnerabilities with a comprehensive, holistic approach ensuring survivors not only regain safety, but also have the chance to thrive again. Our work has been recognized with the Presidential National Award (2017) for launching India’s first hotline to report Child Sexual Abuse Material (CSAM), and the Social Innovation Award (2024) from Pune International Centre for our pioneering efforts in addressing online gender-based violence through Meri Trustline. Job Description: As a Case Manager, you will directly support rehabilitation focused casework interventions for child victims of sexual offences, children at risk, and their families. You will work in a multidisciplinary team of lawyers, social workers and counsellors, in supporting in highly complex and sensitive cases of Child Sexual Abuse. You will report to the Senior Case Worker, and Program Manager and will be expected to bring the highest standards of comprehensive case management support to the most marginalised children and families. Key Responsibilities Working as a part of a multidisciplinary team of social workers, lawyers, and counsellors to support child victims of sexual offences, their families, and other children at risk. Offering support to the child and the family through case management interventions to ensure comprehensive rehabilitation of the child In provision of such support, accompany counsellors/lawyers for conducting home study of victims and families and coordinate with multiple stakeholders that includes police, CWCs, NGOs and other community members. The role is primarily field-based and involves visits to various communities and locations in and around Mumbai. Documentation of case history and all visits conducted in the course of the case. Please note that a specific case management software is used for this purpose. (Training on using the software will be provided) Initiate and draft reports, and other communication with relevant stakeholders, under the guidance of the Senior Case Worker, Program Manager and Director. Liaising with multiple stakeholders: Child Welfare Committees, District Child Protection Units, Police, Hospitals, District Legal Services Authority, other NGOs, judiciary, community members, etc. Handling difficult and emotional situations and/or complaints in a professional, polite, calm and empathetic manner. Uphold strict confidentiality, ethical practices, and child protection protocols. Manage risks and respond effectively in crisis situations. Other duties as assigned, consistent with the above duties as the project develops. Qualifications & Experience: Graduate or or Postgraduate degree in Social Work. Relevant diploma or certificate courses in counselling and legal studies would be an added advantage to the applicants. 5-7 years’ of onground experience in the social work sector is preferred. Fluency in speaking English, Hindi & Marathi. Good writing skills in English. Skilled in documentation, report writing and use of software for case management. A deep commitment to child rights and protection including a non-judgemental attitude, sensitivity and empathy. Self-driven & willing to work as part of a larger team Remuneration: Upto a pproximately ₹ 4.8 lakhs per annum, commensurate with qualifications and experience. Terms of Engagement: This is a full-time position based in Mumbai.and the candidate may be required to undertake field work. RATI works 05 days a week (Monday to Friday) but depending on cases and emergencies, holiday and weekend work may be required. This will be duly compensated. RATI is a new and evolving workspace. We seek colleagues who are adaptable and committed to the cause. As we work with vulnerable women and children, our policies are designed and implemented to ensure the rights and well-being of the women & children we work with are upheld. All employees, without exception, are expected to adhere to these policies. RATI values its team and fosters a supportive and wellbeing-focused work environment. Individuals of all ethnic backgrounds, women, LGBTQIA+ persons and persons with disabilities are strongly encouraged to apply. Administering the Fulbright-Nehru and other fellowships for Indian and American students, faculty, researchers, and professionals; 2. Managing EducationUSA services for Indian students; and 3. Fostering collaborations between higher education institutions in the U.S. and India. Further details are available at www.usief.org.in . This position provides strategic financial leadership by overseeing all accounting and detailed analysis to support effective financial planning and decision-making. This is a full-time position (40 hours per week) based in New Delhi. Monitor risk exposure and mitigation measures and regularly report key risks to the Executive Director. title: Program Director – Medical Services
description: Designation Program Director – Medical Services Location: Ranchi (Jharkhand) / Bhubaneswar (Odisha) / Raipur (Chhattisgarh) / Guwahati (Assam) No. of Vacancies: 5 Project/Unit: Global Alliance for Viksit Bharat (GAVB) Project Background The Global Alliance for Viksit Bharat (GAVB) is a landmark social development initiative designed to uplift 200 million Indians living in multidimensional poverty. With a transformative investment, GAVB concentrates efforts on five priority states—Jharkhand, Assam, Chhattisgarh, Odisha, and Bihar (JACOB states)—which are disproportionately impacted by acute poverty. Health and Education account for 67% of the Multi-dimensional Poverty Index (MDPI). GAVB works closely with state governments to strengthen public health systems, improve service delivery, and enhance community wellbeing. The Communicable Disease (CD) portfolio specifically addresses Tuberculosis (TB) and Malaria—two diseases that disproportionately affect vulnerable populations including tribal communities, urban poor, and migrant workers. GAVB's approach leverages Digitization, Decentralization, Leadership & Institutions, and Inclusion to enhance health service delivery. Domain expertise with proven solutions lays the foundation for introduction, progression, and gradual integration of innovations into government public health systems. Job Summary The Program Director - Medical Services, reporting to the Core Team Member, will anchor facility-based health system transformation in the state, with a focus on improving survival outcomes for mothers, newborns, and critically ill patients. The role will drive the design and institutionalization of high-functioning district hospital and FRU models, ensuring delivery of quality emergency care, optimal utilization of human resources, and strong clinical governance systems - aligned with GAVB’s objective of achieving measurable reductions in maternal and neonatal mortality at scale. The Program Director will lead efforts to build the capacities of medical service cadres through institutions such as SIHFW and SHSRC, while strengthening secondary and tertiary care facilities to deliver comprehensive emergency obstetric and newborn care (CEmONC) and other critical emergency services. The role will also focus on improving quality of care (QoC) through attainment of relevant accreditations, fostering effective partnerships and collaborations across stakeholders, and integrating gender-intentional approaches into policies and program implementation. Additionally, the Program Director will be accountable for end-to-end operational strategy development and execution, ensuring high standards of program quality, and providing strong leadership, direction, and oversight to the team to drive impact at scale. Key Responsibilities 1. Technical Leadership & Strategy Development Design and implement model district hospital and FRU transformation frameworks, including infrastructure, HR deployment, clinical protocols, and governance. Provide technical support to the Health Department to pursue its goals of departmental reorganization for greater effectiveness in attaining long term health goals. Provide evidence-based technical assistance to government and development partners on maternal, newborn and emergency health policies and programs. Support the development and implementation of state and national-level MNH strategies aligned with national guidelines and global best practices. Identify gaps in MNH and emergency services and recommend innovative solutions to enhance service delivery. 2. Program Implementation & Strengthening Assist in designing, implementing, and scaling up high-impact MNH interventions, including antenatal care, skilled birth attendance, emergency obstetric and neonatal care and postnatal care. Support health system strengthening efforts, including quality of care improvements, workforce training and supply chain management for essential MNH commodities. Streamline the support to achieve NQAS, LaQshya certification of targeted facilities as well as FRU functionality. Strengthen one on one and group collaboration among the different partners based on their individual priority areas and objectives. Facilitate existing and new partners in their interactions with the government systems and by making space, facilitating coordination and mutual complementarity. Effectively improve the availability of specialist doctors and their engagement in CEmONC. Along with strengthening the CEmONC services, expand the functional range of emergency services in DHs. Sustain and enhance quality of intrapartum care in block level facilities. Provide on-site technical support to district health officials and frontline workers to improve service delivery. 3. Capacity Building & Training Support designing the content and management of health-related capacity and skill building of cadres through strengthening the SIHFW and its affiliates (RHFWTCs), in close collaboration with partners. Support SHSRC and its linkages to programs (for conducting studies, or engagement of program leadership personnel in SHSRC tasks and support the attendant capacity-building needs). Initiate engagement of medical colleges to support select aspects of the Health System – including capacity building of healthcare providers through the medical colleges on facility organization and service delivery. Internalize clinical mentoring work and strengthen institutional mechanisms for sustaining training and capacity building for nurses and doctors. Facilitate mentorship and supportive supervision mechanisms to enhance the quality of care in hospitals. Strengthen referral systems and emergency response mechanisms for maternal and neonatal complications. 4. Monitoring, Evaluation, and Research Support the development of monitoring and evaluation (M&E) frameworks to track critical health indicators. Facilitate program evaluations, data analysis, and research to assess the impact of interventions and identify areas for improvement. Promote the use of digital health technologies for real-time data collection and decision-making. 5. Policy Influence & Stakeholder Engagement Support the Directorate and SHS to formulate program policies, strategies and guidelines. Engage with donors, partners and academic institutions to align MNH initiatives with national priorities. Influence to unlock increased funding and policy support for maternal and newborn health programs. Contribute to policy briefs, reports, and case studies to inform decision-makers and strengthen evidence-based policymaking. Essential Qualification & Experience MBA/ Masters in Social Work/Public Health/Rural Management/ Hospital Management/ PGDM from Tier-1 institutions (IIMs/ IITs/ MDI etc.) Minimum 10 years of experience in maternal and newborn health, preferably in a public health or development setting. Experience working with government health programs (NHM, RMNCH+A), NGOs, or international agencies. Strong expertise in maternal and neonatal clinical care, health systems strengthening, and program implementation. Proficiency in data analysis, M&E frameworks, and research methodologies. Excellent communication, leadership, and stakeholder engagement skills. Operations management, engagement with government departments, consultancy will be an added advantage. Essential Skills Familiarity with government health policies and programs in India. Experience in designing and implementing health solutions for maternal and newborn care. Ability to work in low-resource settings and travel frequently to field locations. Proficiency in Hindi and English; knowledge of regional languages is a plus. Collaboration with multiple internal/external stakeholders (individual and teams). Experience working in dynamic work environments with substantive dose of ambiguity. Basic level quantitative and qualitative analytical skills.
